title: Bridge sprint launch cribsheet and smoke warmup
body:
Purpose:
Quick cribsheet for the upcoming Bridge Sprint launch window. This doc is a lightweight companion to the full runbook; intended for the ops lane and on-call to run fast checks, warm caches, validate model routing, and execute a controlled traffic ramp with clear rollback triggers. Keep this page pinned in the ops call.

Scope:
- Surface-level checks for production readiness (latency, error budget, endpoints)
- Warmup/priming instructions for KV cache and prefix caching
- A tight T-minus timeline for the 6-hour launch window (evening shift)
- Draft release notes bullets for product & infra teams

Owners and contacts:
- Launch lead: Aisha Patel (owner) slack: @aisha
- Release engineer (night): Diego Morales slack: @diegom
- SRE on-call: Sofia Nguyen slack: @sofiang (pager: PagerDuty SRE rota)
- Model infra lead: Rakesh Iyer slack: @rakesh
- Channel: #ops-bridge-sprint (pin this doc)

Quick timeline (local times UTC):
- T-06:00 (18:00 UTC previous day): final dependency freeze, QA signoff confirmation from product, post merge flags confirmed.
- T-03:00: Dry-run smoke on staging with full traffic simulators (50k RTT samples) — record results.
- T-01:00: Warmup: run prefix-cache priming and KV cache population (procedure below). Confirm KV hit-rate > 70%.
- T-00:30: Run full smoke on canary lane (1% traffic); validate perf & correctness.
- T-00:10: Throttle window open — escalate contacts listed, verify monitoring thresholds.
- T+00:00: Begin 1->5->25->100% ramp per 10m increments, observability checks between each step.
- T+01:00: Stabilize at target traffic, begin telemetry burn-in period (heatmap sampling).
- T+03:00: Post-launch quick retro and ops summary, capture anomalies.

Pre-launch checklist (must be green before T-01:00):
- [ ] All PRs merged & CI green (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pulls)
- [ ] Feature flags created and toggles validated in staging (FF IDs: ff.bridge-sprint, ff.model-fallback)
- [ ] Release artifacts pinned and uploaded to registry (image tags noted in rollout ticket)
- [ ] Database migrations: none OR runbook for DB lock-free migrations validated
- [ ] Capacity: Dedicated cluster autoscaler set to target 120% expected peak; burst policy reviewed
- [ ] Observability: dashboards loaded (#latency-bridge, #error-rates), alerting thresholds copied into temporary watchlist
- [ ] Runbook printout (or local copy) for rollback matrix available to operations

KV cache & prefix warmup procedure (run at T-01:00):
- Purpose: Avoid first-request cold penalty for high-fanout prompt patterns and to reduce initial tail latency.
- Steps:
  1) Obtain warmup payload list: /infra/warmup/bridge_sprint_top_prompts.csv (S3 path)
  2) Run warmup job: infra/warmup-job --target cluster=bridge-prod --concurrency=30 --batch-size=16 --retries=2 --input s3://redwood/warmup/bridge_sprint_top_prompts.csv
  3) Verify KV hit metrics: metrics.kv_cache.hit_rate (target >70%) and metrics.kv_cache.size stable
  4) Run a quick random sample of prompts via canary endpoint and confirm outputs match baseline (checksum attached in warmup job logs)

Canary and routing mapping (what to watch):
- Canary lane (model variant: rwinf-3b-v2-quant) -> route: /v1/gen?model=bridge-canary
- Fallback policy: on latency breach > 400ms p95 OR errors > 0.5% in a window -> auto-route to rwinf-3b-v2 (non-quant) and notify channel with reason code Fallback-01
- Multi-model routing notes: tenant isolation test keys must use test-tenant-42 to verify consistent KV scope

Observability smoke checklist (run at T-00:30 and between ramps):
- [ ] P95 latency below SLA target (configured SLO: 350ms)
- [ ] Error rate < 0.3% on canary endpoints
- [ ] Token-generation CPU/GPU utilization below 80% sustained
- [ ] KV cache hit-rate above warmup threshold
- [ ] No increase in DLQ (dead-letter queue) events for inference-requests topic
- [ ] Trace sampling: ensure end-to-end traces include model selection tag and hw-accelerator id

Rollback matrix (quick reference):
- Severity A (SEV-A): System-wide user-facing errors, error budget exhaustion, sustained p99 > 2x baseline for 10m -> Immediate rollback to previous stable tag, stop traffic ramp, page SRE, open incident channel #inc-bridge-sprint
- Severity B: Canary-level regressions (latency or small functional drift) -> Pause ramp, scale down to canary, hold for 30m for further inspection; if unresolved, rollback canary only
- Severity C: Transient errors < 5m -> Monitor, do not rollback unless persistent or increasing trend

Quick rollback commands (ops):
- Revert to stable tag (k8s): kubectl set image deployment/bridge-service bridge=registry.redwood.ai/bridge:stable-20250211 -n prod
- Route rollback (gateway): curl -X POST $GATEWAY/routing -d '{"route":"stable"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ROUTER_TOKEN'
- Canary disable (feature flag): curl -X POST https://ff.redwood.ai/api/toggle -d '{"ff":"ff.bridge-sprint","state":"off"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $FF_TOKEN'

Post-launch short retro prompts (use in first 60m):
- Did any unexpected traffic routing occur? Where and why?
- Were PV spikes observed in any region or lane?
- Did KV warmup meaningfully reduce tail latency? Attach metrics
- Any uncovered dump or error patterns that need follow-up tickets?

Draft release notes (short bullets for product/marketing):
- Introduced Bridge Sprint optimized variant (rwinf-3b-v2-quant) to reduce per-token cost by ~18% for small-context LLM use-cases.
- Improved routing heuristics to prefer lower-cost variants when latency budget allows.
- Added KV cache warmup jobs to minimize cold-start tail latency for high-volume prefixes.
- Backend: Serving runtime patches to KV eviction policy and batching heuristics (see PR #678).
- No public API changes; SDKs remain compatible.

Open questions / TODOs (capture tasks during ops):
- [ ] Confirm golden-checksum for warmup payloads with model infra (Rakesh)
- [ ] Validate canary telemetry heatmap exporter stability (Diego)
- [ ] Documentation: add short HOWTO for cache warmup to infra handbook
- [ ] Run a targeted load test in eu-west-1 on next maintenance window to exercise regional routing

Appendix: important links & tickets
- Jira: REDWOOD-2148 (bridge-sprint rollout)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/678
- Confluence: release-notes/bridge-sprint-2025-02
- Runbook (full): confluence:runbooks/bridge-sprint-full-runbook

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the 10m ramp conservative; last time we hit a cold cache storm when jumping 1->50%.
- If SLO alerts are chatty at T+00:20, prioritize latency mitigations over functional rollbacks; graceful degradation preferred.
- I want a short graph in the ops channel showing kv_hit_rate + p95 overlay during the ramp.

Last modified notes:
- 2025-02-15: Added KV warmup job flags and success metric targets (Rakesh).
- 2025-02-18: Tightened rollback thresholds after SRE review (Sofia).

End of cribsheet. Keep this doc minimal — link back to full runbook for expanded diagnostics and incident playbook.
